neighbours.label: a degree adjective after 'had a' / 'have a' (a major, a substantial, a huge)
fire: The storm had a huge effect on the harvest that year.
Her coaching had a substantial influence on the young team.
The merger will have a significant cost for local workers.
That decision had a massive role in the company's collapse.
Exercise can have a dramatic benefit for older patients.
The new rules had a considerable impact on prices.
His illness had a profound influence on his later work.
The tax change will have a major consequence for renters.
quiet: The storm hit the coast early in the harvest that year.
Her coaching helped the young team win the cup.
The merger will close two offices for local workers.
That decision came before the company's collapse.
Exercise can help older patients sleep better.
The new rules changed prices across the country.
His illness was mentioned in his later work.
The tax change will apply to renters next year.

notes: probes peaked on ' major' at about 0.23, whether or not 'impact' followed
